blocks.text: THE POINT: this pins LTHR and LT pace properly. Avg HR from minutes 10-30 = LTHR. Avg pace across the 30 ≈ LT pace. Everything downstream in this block inherits these numbers, so a compromised TT is worse than no TT. No hills this week — they start w/c 10 Aug precisely so this stays clean.

BEFORE YOU GO: reset Stryd cal factor 101.7 → 100.0. Comparability with July sessions matters less than a clean anchor. Post-session, compare Garmin distance vs Stryd app distance as the confirmation check. Chest strap on. Same 1km flat straight as 20 Jul — five turnarounds, not the 250m loop.
SCREEN SETUP: HR, 3-second power, elapsed time. HIDE INSTANT PACE. You will chase it otherwise and the first two minutes decide whether the other 28 are any good.

PACING: cap 250W for the first two minutes — cardiac lag is real, the 20 Jul file showed HR at 147 thirty seconds into rep 2 against a 165 steady state, taking ~150s to arrive. First km no faster than 5:40. Then HR-governed: 158-164 to min 5, 164-169 to min 10, 169-173 to min 20, 172-176 to min 27, empty the tank the last three minutes.
EXPECTED: 5.2-5.5 km, power 245W+. If you finish and could have gone harder, log that honestly — it changes how we read the number.

blocks.text: SAT 15 AUG. Sled access day. Sled push and pull remain sandbag friction-overloaded (since 3 Jul) — splits compare to 8 Aug and to each other, NOT to race benchmarks.

THE REVISED BIRMINGHAM MECHANISM — read this before you start. Race-file HR: Run 1 143.5 -> SkiErg 128.1 -> roxzone 120.8 -> Run 2 at 5:03/km, THE SAME PACE AS RUN 1, HR 150.8 -> Sled Push 5:14 of work against 2:59 at Cardiff -> every run after pinned 178-182. HR fell through the ski because SkiErg is upper-body and non-weight-bearing; it built a lactate cost the HR trace could not show. The ski loaded it. RUN 2 AT UNCHANGED PACE IS THE DECISION THAT SPENT IT. The sled push is where the time went.

REMOVED FROM THE 8 AUG BRIEF: 'can you hold run 1 pace straight off the ski'. That instruction rehearsed the failure. Run 2 is held at CONTROLLED pace regardless of how good the ski felt. That restraint is the skill being trained.

PEAK HR IS NOT THE METRIC. On 8 Aug the runs held 253-258W against CP 261 — 97-99% of threshold power — and still capped at HR 162, because a 3:00 block never lets HR arrive. Peak HR here measures block length, not effort.

SUCCESS CRITERIA, in order: (1) SLED PUSH SPLIT — the primary readout, the station that collapsed at Birmingham. (2) RESTART HR — HR at the top of run 4 no more than 6 bpm above the top of run 2. (3) FOUR RUN SPLITS INSIDE 5 SECONDS. (4) RATCHET SHAPE — you want climb-then-hold, roughly 155 -> 165 -> 170 -> 170. Climbing and still climbing at run 4 means you are rehearsing Birmingham. On 8 Aug it read 147 -> 158 -> 162 -> 162, which decelerated into a plateau at 162; the target band for a well-executed race is 168-174.
SKI: one notch harder than 8 Aug, not two. The 8 Aug PWA RPE was 7, not the 4 the old file recorded. Enough to leave a real cost, not enough to reproduce the failure.

RUN PACE: 5:25-5:35/km = 10.8-11.1 km/h, roughly 248-256W at CP 261. START RUN 1 AT 10.8. On 8 Aug you started at 10.98 and the two slowest runs followed — 16s spread across four when the stated test was four flat.
STATION EXPOSURE: 8 Aug logged SkiErg 3:10 / Sled Push 2:52 / Sled Pull 3:06 / BBJ 3:00 = 12:08. This week should read ~16:00. Log it — RSS scores station work at ~0W and cannot see these minutes.

blocks.text: WED 19 AUG @ RAW. THE SESSION YOU HAVE NEVER DONE. In seven weeks since 2 Jul the race has been trained as two halves that never meet - stations 1-4 in the sims, 5-8 in the chain. Birmingham's collapse started in the front half and propagated into the back. This tests the join, at full race distance.
MOVED FROM SAT 22 AUG - you are at the Corporate Games Fri-Sun. Built by extending Wednesday's 100% chain forwards rather than shrinking it, so stations 5-8 keep full race volume.

WHAT YOU GAVE UP TO GET THIS, so it is not a surprise afterwards: this is NOT a repeat of 12 Aug. The lunge arrives with SEVEN stations behind it instead of three, so a slower split than 6:39 is expected and correct, and there is no clean baseline to read it against. The 12 Aug comparison is gone until sharpen week. That was the trade.

RUN PACE 5:45-5:50/km, ALL EIGHT. Agreed compromise off 5:35. Runs controlled, stations attacked - the standing race rule. RUN 2 IS HELD AT RUN 1 PACE regardless of how the ski felt. That restraint is the skill being trained; holding pace off the ski at Birmingham is the decision that spent the race.

HEAT RULE. 12 Aug ran at 32C in an unventilated unit. 45 min at 32C is hard; 90+ min at 32C is a different category and is a heat problem, not a training problem. LOG THE TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU START. If it is near 32C, drop stations 1-4 to HALF distance and keep 5-8 full. Do not attempt the full version in that heat.

SPINAL CHECKPOINTS on Sled Pull, Farmers Carry, Sandbag Lunge and Wall Balls - effort and symptom as SEPARATE numbers, logged immediately, free-texted because of the app floor defect. SYMPTOM RPE ABOVE 2 STOPS THE SESSION MID-STATION. Station 7 at full volume with seven stations behind it is the highest spinal exposure of the entire block - this is the single most likely place it shows up, and the rule does not soften because the session is interesting.
Sleds remain friction-overloaded (10 kg sandbag dragged in front, astroturf). Splits compare to 8 and 15 Aug, NOT to race benchmarks.

SUCCESS CRITERIA, in order: (1) completion without a symptom stop; (2) run 8 within 15 seconds of run 1; (3) where the HR trace plateaus - that number is your real race ceiling; (4) the full 1000m ski split, for calibration against the effort-6 700m extrapolation; (5) sled push split, the station that collapsed at Birmingham. blocks.text: SAT 29 AUG @ RAW. START AT 15:10 to mirror the Tenerife race window. Unventilated unit. LOG THE TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU START.

Different pacing problem - you go harder per segment because rest is coming, and misjudging that is the mistake available in Tenerife. Chris is unavailable, so this is solo.

REVISED UP from 6:30-6:50 after meeting Chris on 21 Aug - his repeatable ceiling now reads ~5:50/km, and race average is projected 6:15-6:45/km compromised in afternoon heat. 6:10-6:20 is the honest midpoint. DO NOT DRIFT DOWN TO 5:45 BECAUSE IT FEELS COMFORTABLE. Running your pace instead of his is the exact failure mode on the day, and the doubles rule is a 1-minute penalty per separation, out of competition after three. STANDING RACE RULE: Chris sets the pace on every run. JJ never leads.

STATIONS AT ~60% OF RACE VOLUME. 60/40 not 50/50 - Chris is a first-timer and taking the larger share is the honest planning assumption. REST IS TIMED ON A CLOCK, STANDING, NEVER SITTING. Self-selected rest is always longer than a partner's segment and it makes the session worthless. Doubles rules require the resting athlete on their feet in the workout zone - practise that too.

SEATED PROTOCOL: get up and walk every 45-60 min. On arrival, walk 10-15 min BEFORE you sit down again. No standing toe touches, no seated forward folds to 'stretch it out' - that is the exact mechanism to avoid.

blocks.text: NUTRITION: ~400 g carbohydrate. Second day of the load. Airport and in-flight food is the failure point - carry your own. No seafood.
HYDRATION: flights are dehydrating and you are racing into 26-28C at 68-82% humidity. Add electrolytes today and tomorrow morning, not just water.
ON ARRIVAL, CHECK IN PERSON - these could not be answered from the UK: BBJ lane length, SkiErg and Row entrance/exit mat transit distances, venue floor surface. All three change the split maths.

IF ANY WINDOW WITH CHRIS EXISTS TONIGHT OR TOMORROW MORNING, TAKE IT. Even 20 minutes of YGIG on two stations to agree who calls the swap is worth more than anything else available. You have never rehearsed a single transition together and that is the largest uncontrolled variable in this race.

FRI 4 SEP. HYROX TENERIFE, DOUBLES with Chris. Start 15:10. THIS IS A DRESS REHEARSAL, NOT A TARGET RACE. Birmingham on 31 Oct is the priority. Projected team finish 1:30-1:36 and that number is not the point.

STANDING RACE RULE, non-negotiable: CHRIS SETS THE PACE ON EVERY RUN. JJ NEVER LEADS. His repeatable ceiling is ~5:50/km and race average is projected 6:15-6:45/km compromised in the afternoon heat. Separation is a 1-minute penalty each time and out of competition after three.

RUN-2 RULE STILL APPLIES, even in doubles. Whatever the SkiErg felt like, run 2 goes deliberately slower than run 1. Birmingham 2025 ran run 2 at identical pace to run 1 (5:03/km) and paid for it at the Sled Push - 5:14, 96.5th percentile. Control runs by LAP TIME, not the pace display.

YGIG: resting athlete stays ON THEIR FEET in the workout zone. No kneeling, sitting or lying down. Both enter and both leave together. Take the larger share where it is cheap for you and the smaller share where it is not - Chris is a first-timer and the wall balls at the end are where a first-timer breaks.
SPINAL CHECKPOINTS remain live IN THE RACE: Farmers Carry, Sandbag Lunge, Wall Balls. Symptom RPE above 2 is a hard stop and it is still a hard stop on race day. This race is not worth Birmingham.
HEAT: 26-28C at 68-82% humidity with a 15:10 start. Pre-cool if there is shade and ice available. Drink at every roxzone pass rather than banking it.

LOG AFTERWARDS: all eight run splits, station work times, roxzone entry/exit, three spinal checkpoint pairs, temperature, and honest notes on the transitions with Chris. The transition data is the single most valuable thing this race produces for Birmingham.
SAT 5 SEP. FULL REST. 20-40 min easy walking is good, nothing else. No stretching into flexion after a race - the discs have taken 90 minutes of loaded work.
Eat and rehydrate properly. Protein 155 g minimum today.
Write the race notes TODAY while they are fresh, especially the transitions and anything Chris said about pacing. Memory of a race decays within 48h and the Birmingham build is built on it.

SUN 6 SEP. Optional 20-30 min very easy jog, HR <=140. Take it if the legs are fine, skip it without guilt if they are not. QUICK BOUNCE-BACK, NOT A DEEP DELOAD - the Birmingham build starts tomorrow and it is only eight weeks.

blocks.label: Optional shakeout
blocks.detail: 20-30 min very easy, HR <=140

blocks.text: WEEKLY PLANNING SESSION - this one is the big one. Build w/c 7 Sep onward against the LOCKED Option B running ladder (agreed 12 Aug): w/c 7 Sep 25 km, 14 Sep 29 km, 21 Sep 33 km (incl 5x1km @ 4:55), 28 Sep 24 km deload (Preston 10k 27 Sep, FULL race effort), 5 Oct 36 km, 12 Oct 40 km peak (CTL ~39-41), then 19 and 26 Oct taper into Birmingham 31 Oct.

BUILD INTO w/c 7 Sep ONWARD: (1) VO2max slot - the current block has been threshold-heavy with no VO2max work at all due to back caution, and the deleted hills session rolls into here; (2) unilateral reintroduction - split squats, single-leg calf raise, Bulgarian split squat, single-arm farmers carry, barbell RDL, now that the pre-Tenerife patterning phase is over; (3) Wednesday strength slots; (4) core moves back to Tuesday AND Thursday and starts progressing again.

RE-TEST CP: 30-minute TT in w/c 7 or 14 Sep. Field data from this block (17 Aug intervals 264-293W, 24 Aug 268W at RPE 6.5) says true CP is modestly above the stored 261W. Do not update the anchor before the TT. The Preston 10k target of 4:50/km is CONDITIONAL on that TT returning high AND the 5x1km @ 4:55 session going cleanly w/c 21 Sep - otherwise the defensible target stays 5:00-5:05/km.

RAMP RULE WARNING for the w/c 7 Sep build: measure the post-race ramp against the PRE-taper week (w/c 24 Aug, ~350), NOT against the taper week. Measuring off the deload week will incorrectly block a normal return to load.

prerun.text: PRE-RUN — ~9 min, in order. Spine-neutral throughout: no standing toe touches, no seated forward folds, no supine knees-to-chest. Press START on the first step, it auto-advances the whole routine.

prerun.label: Knee-to-wall dorsiflexion
prerun.detail: 10 reps/side, 2s hold at end range. Heel down, knee over 2nd toe. Switch at halfway. Note the L/R gap difference.

prerun.label: Ankle circles
prerun.detail: 20 each direction, both sides. Slow, full range.

prerun.label: Bent-knee heel raise
prerun.detail: 15 reps, 2s lower. Soleus — takes the running load, don't skip it.

prerun.label: Single-leg balance hold
prerun.detail: 20s on the weaker ankle only. Eyes open.

prerun.label: Half-kneeling hip flexor
prerun.detail: 30s/side. Squeeze the down-leg glute, tuck the pelvis. Do NOT arch the back to feel it.

prerun.label: 90/90 hip switches
prerun.detail: 8 slow reps. Sit tall, hands behind, chest up. Stop short if the low back rounds to get there.

prerun.label: Leg swings (wall support)
prerun.detail: 12 front/back then 12 lateral per side. Small range first 4, then build. Swing from the hip, trunk braced.

prerun.label: Glute bridge
prerun.detail: 15 reps, 2s squeeze at top, ribs down.

prerun.label: Banded lateral walk
prerun.detail: 10 steps each direction x2. Band above knees, soft knees, no torso lean.

prerun.label: Pogo hops
prerun.detail: 2 x 15. Stiff ankles, minimal knee bend, short ground contact. SKIP on easy days or if flat.

core.text: CORE / TRUNK ENDURANCE - ~16 min. Anti-movement only: resist flexion, extension, rotation and lateral flexion, never produce them. PERMANENTLY OUT with the annular tear: sit-ups, crunches, V-ups, toes-to-bar, GHD sit-ups, weighted Russian twists, loaded side bends, hanging leg raises with a rounded lumbar spine. Repeated end-range loaded lumbar flexion is the specific mechanism that drives nuclear material posteriorly through an annular defect.
TIMING: not within the first hour of waking. Discs are maximally hydrated overnight and the spine is at its most flexion-vulnerable then. Mid-morning or later.

PART A - McGill Big 3, descending pyramid 6 -> 4 -> 2 reps. Every rep is a 10-second hold, ~5s between reps, ~30s between sets. Log effort and symptom RPE as SEPARATE numbers per exercise. Symptom RPE above 2 during or after = hard stop, same rule as the stations.

core.label: Modified curl-up - 6/4/2
core.detail: Hands flat UNDER the lumbar spine, one knee bent one leg straight. Lift head and shoulders barely off the floor - you are bracing, not crunching. No spinal flexion. Swap the bent leg between sets. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

core.label: Side plank - 6/4/2 per side
core.detail: From the knees if the full version provokes anything. Complete the full pyramid on one side, then the other. Straight line ear-to-hip, ribs down, no sagging or hitching. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

core.label: Bird dog - 6/4/2
core.detail: Opposite arm and leg, 10s hold, alternate sides within the rep count. Broomstick-flat lumbar spine - do NOT arch to reach further. Reach long, not high. SPINAL CHECKPOINT.

core.text: PART B - loaded anti-movement, 3 sets each. Band or cable. This is the part that progresses by load; Part A progresses by duration only.

core.label: Pallof press - 3 x 8-10/side
core.detail: Stand side-on to the anchor, band at sternum height. Press to full extension and hold 3 seconds resisting the rotation, then return under control. Hips square, no leaning away from the pull.

core.label: Dead bug w/ overhead band - 3 x 8/side
core.detail: Arms hold band tension overhead, ribs pinned down, low back flat to the floor. Lower opposite arm and leg slowly. If the back lifts off the floor, shorten the range - that is the rep limit, not a cue to push through.

core.text: PROGRESSION, in this order and one at a time: (1) pyramid to 8/6/4, (2) holds 10s -> 12s, (3) more band tension on Part B. Never add external load to the Big 3. HOLD STEADY through the w/c 31 Aug deload+taper - that is not the place for a new stimulus. Progress from the Birmingham build, w/c 7 Sep.
